_comment: Two-tier v2 S5 diagnostic L1b (2026-09-17, after the L1 campaign's short-horizon readout): every L1 arm reads its truth waypoint token and ignores it — truth-plan and no-plan ADE[0,60] within 2-4 m on all six main arms (pa_s1337 fixed anchor: 181 / 183 m vectored), and a token whose waypoints are shifted 2 km north moves the 60 s endpoint by 67 m (p50, 48 val flights; 2 km up: 161 m). The head's no-plan reading beats native32 cut at 60 s (136 vs 163 m at the fixed anchor, 77 vs 136 at 8 km), so it is a good short-horizon predictor that never learned to steer to a given waypoint. Four single-seed arms on the path-angle contract isolate the optimisation levers before any architecture change: the 50 % token dropout off (the head sees the token on every row), the LR plateau cuts off (the L1 arms' rate fell from 3e-5 to 1e-7 by epoch ~126 under patience 3 on a noisy objective, so most of the 180 epochs trained at nothing), both, and dropout off with the smoothness terms (heading-rate 8, bank TV 1) off so the position term is the objective. Same cohort, anchor and readouts as the L1 campaign (`short_horizon_readout` against native32; the truth-plan against no-plan pairing is the reading). A head that follows its token shows truth-plan ADE[0,60] well below no-plan and an endpoint that moves with a shifted token; if none of the four does, the token needs a direct pathway into the control head (an architecture change, the user's call).

arms.label: path-angle, token dropout 0 (the token on every row)
path-angle, dropout 0.5, no LR plateau cuts
path-angle, dropout 0 + no LR plateau cuts
path-angle, dropout 0 + heading-rate and bank-TV terms off
